subject: RE: AltoBank - request for residency / erasure artifacts for SOC2 audit
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@altobank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: KPMG SOC2 <soc2@kpmg.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Data residency & erasure artifacts - AltoBank SOC2 audit

Hi Marcus,

We're kicking off the AltoBank portion of our SOC2 scope and KPMG asked us to gather concrete artifacts showing how Redwood handles tenant residency, retention TTLs, and deletion proof for customer data. Can you please provide the following by COB Thursday?

1) Short description of where customer data resides (primary region + any geo-replicas) and an export mapping for AltoBank tenant ID AB-2026-07.
2) The retention/TTL policy excerpt that applies to tenant data and any automated deletion workflows.
3) A small sample of audit logs or evidence showing a completed deletion event (redacted tenant identifiers ok) plus timestamps.
4) Any attestation language you use to confirm deletion completion (we can include in the SOC2 packet).

If you have a single package or playbook that bundles these artifacts that would be ideal. Also happy to take a 30-minute walkthrough if that speeds things up — availability this week is limited but we can try to find a slot.

Attached is our initial intake spreadsheet to capture the mapping (request_initial_spec.xlsx).

Thanks,
Elaine
AltoBank — InfoSec

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@altobank.com>
Cc: KPMG SOC2 <soc2@kpmg.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:12 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: Data residency & erasure artifacts - AltoBank SOC2 audit

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. We're compiling the artifacts and I can get an initial package to you by end of day Wednesday. Quick summary below and items I'll attach: 

- Residency: Primary tenant data for AB-2026-07 is provisioned in us-west-2. We maintain asynchronous cross-region replication to us-east-1 for failover; no copies are kept outside defined regions. (More detail in the mapping CSV.)
- Retention/TTL: Default object TTL for tenant data is 90 days unless contractually overridden; metadata and indexes follow a 180-day archival TTL.
- Deletion workflow: We run a multi-step erasure workflow (mark -> background purge -> verify KVS tombstone removal -> audit mark).

Attachments (stubs): redwood_erasure_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook excerpt), ttl_config_snapshot_2026-11.yml (policy snapshot). I'll also include a sample audit CSV from a scrub run in our staging tenant that mirrors AltoBank's schema.

If KPMG needs an attestation draft, I can propose language and route through legal. Want me to include a rough attestation doc for AltoBank to review?

If it helps, I'm available for a 30-min sync Wednesday 14:00-16:00 PT — let me know if that works for your team.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
[attachment: redwood_erasure_playbook_v1.pdf (pdf)]
[attachment: ttl_config_snapshot_2026-11.yml (yaml)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:25:40 -0800
Subject: Fw: AltoBank - request for residency / erasure artifacts for SOC2 audit

Neha/Irene — forwarding AltoBank's request. Can you help pull the artifacts below? We need redacted samples that are audit-friendly (timestamps, operation IDs, and verification hashes are fine; tenant UUIDs can be masked). Specific asks: 

- Neha: please export a redacted sample_audit_log_ALTO_AB-2026-07.csv showing a completed purge run (include event IDs and verification status). Confirm time zone normalization and whether we can include request callids.
- Irene: please pull the TTL configuration snapshot and the shortest attestation text we usually provide. Also confirm whether KMS key lifecycle events (log excerpts) exist for the purge run.

Deadline: COB Wednesday (2026-12-02) — AltoBank indicated they want artifacts Wednesday/Thursday. I'll bundle and send to Elaine + KPMG.

Thanks — Marcus

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:17:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Fw: AltoBank - request for residency / erasure artifacts for SOC2 audit

Hi Marcus — putting the deliverables here. I generated the sample log from a scrub run (dev mirror AB-2026-07) and redacted tenant IDs per legal's guidance. Files attached as stubs below. Notes: 

- sample_audit_log_ALTO_AB-2026-07.csv — contains event_timestamp (UTC), operation_id, stage (marked/purged/verified), verifier_id, verification_hash. We redacted internal IPs and full tenant UUIDs.
- ttl_config_snapshot_2026-11.yml — shows the 90-day object TTL and 180-day metadata TTL; includes flag for contract overrides.
- kms_key_deletion_events_excerpt.log — excerpt with kmsKeyId and deletion confirmation events; redacted principal ARNs.

Caveats: the KMS deletion log is our control-plane event stream and shows a deletion confirmation but does not include raw envelope keys. For SOC2 proof the auditors tend to accept the event excerpt plus our verification hash mapping.

Links: I've uploaded the source artifacts to the internal folder: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/erasure-playbook-AB

Will stand by for any follow-ups.

—Neha

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fw: AltoBank - request for residency / erasure artifacts for SOC2 audit

Marcus/Neha — couple of notes before we hand this to AltoBank / KPMG: 

1) Attestation wording: propose we use a short, explicit statement that references the tenant identifier, the deletion workflow run id, and a verification hash. Draft in attestation_draft_altobank.docx. Keep it narrowly scoped to avoid legal exposure.
2) Cross-region copies: confirm we include the replication snapshot evidence showing the same purge run propagated to us-east-1. I pulled a replication confirmation table and attached an excerpt replication_confirmation_us-east-1.csv.
3) Timeline: ensure the audit CSV shows both the mark and final verification timestamps — auditors will check for monotonic progression.

I'll attach my redline of the attestation and a short checklist we can add to the SOC2 packet.

Irene
Senior Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
